title: Heat conversion
meaning: Wet volume becomes dry mass, then fuel energy, then useful heat.

title: Delivered volume and useful heat
meaning: Trucks deliver whole loads. Both material streams use the same plant-specific coefficient.

title: Cost minimization
meaning: Pay for delivered dry biomass and useful gas heat. Opening stock is already on hand.

title: Post-solve emissions
meaning: Gas is counted once per day. Factors describe a stated useful-heat basis. Emissions do not influence dispatch.

title: Shared fuel availability
meaning: Both plants draw from the same delivered and stored pools. Summing first prevents double claims.

title: Inventory conservation
meaning: Opening stock plus deliveries equals burn plus closing stock. The formulation has no disposal or storage loss.

title: Stock boundaries
meaning: Opening stock is an input. The optional final target applies to each fuel at the horizon.

title: Shared truck limit
meaning: Fuel types compete for receiving slots.

title: Storage and optional pellet cap
meaning: The pellet silo is interpreted as a pellet-only sublimit within total closing storage.

title: Plant capacity
meaning: Each plant has a separate useful heat limit.

title: Demand balance
meaning: The two biomass plants and gas together meet each day's demand exactly.

title: Optional gas limit
meaning: Gas is uncapped where no supply cap has been provided.

title: Domains
meaning: The MILP rounds no physical fuel flows. Only the truck decisions are integer-constrained.
